subject: english-language
source_note: Topic structure follows the OCR GCSE English Language specification. Connections, sequence and prerequisites are expert-authored teaching relationships (exam boards do not publish these).

units.name: Communicating Information and Ideas
units.blurb: Reading non-fiction and writing for audience, impact and purpose (Component 01)

units.name: Exploring Effects and Impact
units.blurb: Reading literary prose and writing imaginatively and creatively (Component 02)

units.name: Spoken Language Endorsement
units.blurb: Presenting, responding and using spoken Standard English (Component 03/04)

topics.name: Reading & Comparing Non-Fiction Texts
topics.blurb: Two unseen non-fiction texts, one 19th-century and one 20th/21st-century

topics.name: Analysing Language & Structure in Non-Fiction
topics.blurb: How writers use language and structure to inform and persuade

topics.name: Comparing & Evaluating Texts
topics.blurb: Synthesise, compare and evaluate two texts against a given statement

topics.name: Writing Original Non-Fiction
topics.blurb: One transactional/persuasive piece for a set audience, impact and purpose

topics.name: Reading & Comparing Literary Prose
topics.blurb: Two unseen prose texts (fiction or literary non-fiction), 20th/21st-century

topics.name: Analysing Language, Structure & Effects
topics.blurb: How writers achieve effects and influence readers (AO2)

topics.name: Comparing & Evaluating Effects
topics.blurb: Compare and evaluate two prose texts in response to a statement

topics.name: Imaginative & Creative Writing
topics.blurb: One original creative piece, often with an open form or audience

topics.name: Preparing & Delivering a Presentation
topics.blurb: A prepared talk, debate, speech or dialogue on an agreed topic (AO7)

topics.name: Responding to Questions & Feedback
topics.blurb: Listen and respond appropriately to questions and feedback (AO8)

topics.name: Using Spoken Standard English
topics.blurb: Use spoken Standard English effectively in speeches and presentations (AO9)

connections.why: Close reading of non-fiction is the basis for analysing how its language and structure work
Identifying a writer's techniques is the first step before comparing and evaluating two texts
Comparison requires confident reading of both the 19th- and 20th/21st-century texts together
Understanding how professionals craft non-fiction equips students to write their own
Evaluating what makes a text effective sharpens choices about purpose, impact and audience in writing
Reading prose closely is the foundation for analysing the effects writers create
Analysing each text's effects enables a comparison and evaluation of their impact
Evaluating against a statement depends on reading both prose texts attentively
Studying how writers build atmosphere and effect models the craft of imaginative writing
Judging what makes prose powerful informs students' own creative choices
Core reading skills transfer across non-fiction and literary prose components
Language and structure analysis is a shared skill applied to both non-fiction and fiction
The comparison and evaluation skill is assessed across both reading papers
Both writing tasks share command of structure, vocabulary and technical accuracy
Shaping non-fiction for an audience and purpose mirrors planning a persuasive spoken presentation
Crafting language for impact in writing transfers to engaging an audience when speaking
Knowing rhetorical and persuasive devices helps students deploy them in their own speeches
A clear presentation sets up the discussion in which students respond to questions and feedback
Delivering a presentation requires sustained, effective use of spoken Standard English
Responding spontaneously still demands controlled, accurate spoken Standard English
